# kapsel-diag golden `real-check`. Regenerate with KAPSEL_BLESS=1.
# file: script.sh
--- input
false || true
cat missing.txt | sort
jq . a.json
--- output
error[KS-R001]: `|| true` turns any failure of the command before it into success and destroys the error signal; handle the failure explicitly, e.g. `|| echo ...`
 --> script.sh:1:7
  |
1 | false || true
  |       ^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: `|| true` hides the exit status the next step or the caller needs to know the work failed (REQ-KS-012)
  = help: handle the failure explicitly: `cmd || { echo 'cmd failed, continuing because ...' >&2; }`, or drop the `|| true`

warning[KS-R016]: `cat missing.txt` reads a path that may not exist in a pipeline stage that is not the last, so a failure here cannot change the pipeline's status
 --> script.sh:2:5
  |
2 | cat missing.txt | sort
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: the status of a pipeline is its last stage, so a missing path in an earlier stage prints an error and still exits 0 (187 measured)
  = help: test the path first (`[ -e missing.txt ] &&`) or make it the last stage

error[KS-R009]: `jq` is not a kapsel built-in and is refused; native tools arrive in v0.5 (REQ-KS-030)
 --> script.sh:3:1
  |
3 | jq . a.json
  | ^^
  |
  = note: every command is compiled to a WASM component and run in a sandbox; programs outside the built-in list need native tools, planned for v0.5 (REQ-KS-030)
  = help: jq: use `json get PATH FILE` (`-r` raw strings, `-c` compact), `json set PATH VALUE FILE`, `json del PATH FILE` or `json merge FILE OTHER`; other uses of `jq` need native tools (v0.5, REQ-KS-030)

error: refused: 2 errors, 1 warning
